basis: Aortic and skeletal disease characterize the common subtypes; Marfan predominates and has lens dislocation in about 60%.
Inherited renal tubular dysfunction causes defining hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis; muscle spasms do not establish muscle damage.
Optic atrophy with visual loss defines the disease; headache does not establish additional neurologic damage.
Lissencephaly, callosal agenesis and epilepsy define the disorder; malabsorption occurs in 30-79%. Cardiac and exocrine pancreatic defects occur in 5-29%.
A disorder of lipoprotein metabolism; altered coronary risk does not establish cardiovascular damage.
Inherited ventricular electrical dysfunction causes ventricular fibrillation; syncope does not establish neurologic injury.
Fatty acid and amino acid oxidation disorder; myopathy with proximal weakness and elevated CK occurs in 30-79%. Hepatic and cardiac damage is occasional across the umbrella.
Hypomyelinating CNS disease; optic atrophy in 2/6 and visual impairment in 3/6 support ocular involvement; joint contractures occur in 2/6.
Abnormal indolylacroylglycine metabolism with defining intellectual disability; urinary metabolite excretion does not establish kidney damage.
Hypopituitarism and limb malformations define the syndrome. Unspecified midline malformations do not securely establish another organ axis.
Defining bradykinin-mediated edema affects subcutis, bowel and upper airway. C1-inhibitor dysfunction does not itself establish immunodeficiency or autoimmune disease.
Congenital vertebral segmentation abnormalities define the disease; spinal canal stenosis alone does not establish neurologic damage.
Myeloid neoplasm of blood and marrow with persistent monocytosis and myelodysplasia; no common extrahematologic organ damage established.
Defective T-cell immune function defines an immunodeficiency; no cytopenia or specific damaged organ is established.
Air occupies the pleural cavity and compromises lung expansion; infectious causes apply only to particular subtypes.
The syndrome is defined by sensorineural hearing loss, retinal pigment epithelium lesions and abnormal tooth coloration; teeth map to gastrointestinal.
Pancreatic insulin dysregulation causes hypoglycemia. Specific lasting neurologic deficits occur in 5-29%; the broad nervous-system annotation does not establish lasting damage.
An inborn glycosylation disorder; developmental neurologic impairment is common (>30%) across the defective-fucosylation subtypes.
Red-cell membrane disease causes hemolytic anemia; splenic involvement remains on the blood axis. Jaundice is not liver injury; gallstones are a separate disease.
Congenital atrial septal defect is the defining structural cardiac lesion, present in 20/20 annotated patients.
Cirrhosis, muscle weakness and spasticity each occur in 2/2. Cardiac, renal and exocrine pancreatic dysfunction each occur in 1/2 and are omitted at the four-axis cap.
Skeletal anomalies and hearing loss define it; intellectual disability occurs in 8/10 and cardiac anomalies in 30-79%. Ptosis and nail defects (30-79%) omitted at cap.
Carcinoma in situ originates in the pharynx, which maps to the pulmonary axis under these rules.
Propionate metabolism defect; developmental and cognitive neurologic impairment affects over 50%. Cardiomyopathy generally affects fewer than 30%.
Opisthorchis flukes inhabit and inflame the biliary tract; cholangiocarcinoma is a later risk and separate disease.
